newsitem.title: UK: Blair to break precedent, visit UK by-election.
newsitem.headline: Blair to break precedent, visit UK by-election.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair is to break precedent on Friday by campaigning for the Labour candidate battling to win a Conservative seat at the Uxbridge parliamentary by-election, Labour sources said on Wednesday.
They said Blair rejected conventional wisdom that Prime Ministers should not take part in by-elections because defeat would then be seen as a personal reflection on them.
"The argument is that defeat is seen as a defeat for the party leader. But that happens anyway," one source said.

He quoted Blair as having declared: "I am the elected prime minister and it is my government that is seeking the approval of the people of Uxbridge on July 31. That is why I will visit the constituency myself."

Labour's Andrew Slaughter is fighting to overcome a Conservative majority of 724 in the first by-election of the new parliament, caused by the death a few days after the May 1 general election of Conservative Michael Shersby.
The sources said Labour canvass returns in Uxbridge, a town on the western fringes of London, showed the result was on a knife-edge.
They said the absence of a candidate for the Referendum Party, which polled 1,153 votes at the general election, made Slaughter's task more difficult. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
